assumptions: JUCHMME's trained 114-state model applies to this protein's family.
The host has loaded the trained model; without it the tool says so.
limits: A posterior per residue is the model's confidence, not an experimental topology.
Signal peptides can be mistaken for helices, which the labelled path shows.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which residues of this protein are inside, in a transmembrane helix, or outside, by the HMM-TM model?

description: Transmembrane topology of a protein by the HMM-TM 114-state hidden Markov model (JUCHMME, Bagos et al.), decoded residue by residue into inside / transmembrane-helix / outside runs. Reports the labelled path, the runs as residue spans, and the per-residue posterior. Needs the trained model, which the host loads once per session — this refuses by name when it has not been.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

decoding.description: which decoder: 'viterbi' the single most probable state path (default, and the fast one); 'posterior-viterbi' and 'optimal-accuracy' re-decode over the posterior; 'n-best' beams over label SEQUENCES rather than states and is a genuinely different algorithm — and much slower on a long chain.

protein.description: the protein sequence (unambiguous one-letter codes); wire it from translate_sequence.

name: protein_topology

helices.description: how many runs are transmembrane helices — 0 means no helix was predicted, which for a cytosolic protein is the right answer and not a failure

logProb.description: log probability of the decoded path, in nats

path.description: one label per residue, in sequence order

posterior.description: per-residue posterior probability of each label — the confidence behind the path

segments.description: runs of one label as 1-based inclusive residue spans

summary.description: the topology in words — how many helices and which side the N-terminus is on, or that none was predicted
